curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: adopt reading pictures and textsfor enjoyment and information.

interactions.prompt: A picture shows children laughing on swings. Why might you look at it?
interactions.feedback: Yes! A cheerful picture can be enjoyed.
interactions.retryHint: Think about how the laughing children make a reader feel.

interactions.prompt: Read the sign: “Library opens at 8.” What information does it give?
interactions.feedback: Great! The text tells when the library opens.
interactions.retryHint: Look for the number and what it tells us.

interactions.prompt: Match each reading item to its main purpose.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap an item, then tap why someone might read it.
interactions.feedback: Well done! Reading can delight us, teach us, or do both.
interactions.retryHint: Ask whether each item is fun, useful for facts, or both.

interactions.prompt: A poster shows a tap and says, “Wash hands before eating.” What should the reader learn?
interactions.feedback: Correct! The picture and words share useful health information.
interactions.retryHint: Use both the tap picture and the written message.

interactions.prompt: A page shows dark clouds. The text says, “Kito carries an umbrella.” What can you work out?
choices: It is a hot, cloudless day
interactions.feedback: Excellent! You joined the picture clue and text clue.
interactions.retryHint: What weather often comes with dark clouds and an umbrella?

interactions.prompt: Sort what each reader gains from the item.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap an item, then tap enjoyment, information, or both.
interactions.feedback: Super! You know that pictures and texts can be read for fun and facts.
interactions.retryHint: Think about whether the item makes reading fun, gives useful facts, or does both.
